episode.project: A single-channel stage-lighting toolkit using integer time units: run-length compaction of per-channel level samples, greedy non-overlapping scheduling of named cues with requested starts and durations, and an integration step that renders both results together.

source_messages.text: Welcome to the lighting project. module.py holds a tiny validated helper plus three stubs we'll grow into a cue compaction and scheduling pipeline; times and durations are plain integers. Two standing rules for any function you write or edit in this project: 1) Whenever an argument doesn't match the documented valid shape, return exactly the string "invalid" — never null, and never raise. 2) Whenever you have to order items that compare equal on the ordering key, keep the order they first appeared in the input. These rules attach when a function is written or edited; I'll never silently expect you to rewrite earlier working functions when rules evolve.

One open choice, also standing: a compacted run may be represented either as a two-item list [level, count] or as an object {"level": <int>, "count": <int>}. Both are acceptable anywhere runs are produced — pick whichever you prefer; tests accept both.

request.text: Time to fill in compact_cue(payload) in module.py. It takes one argument: a list of light-level samples for one channel, where every sample must be a JSON integer (booleans are not integers here). Compact it into runs of equal consecutive values: return one run per maximal block of equal neighbors, each run recording that block's value and how many samples it contains, with runs in the order they occur. An empty list compacts to an empty list. Anything that isn't a valid sample list counts as invalid input — follow our standing rules for that, and for how runs may be represented. Submit just the new compact_cue definition.

(2) Global, permitted — run representation: each produced run may be a two-element list [level, count] or an object {"level": ..., "count": ...}; both are always acceptable and neither is mandatory. No task-local override exists. The global first-seen tie rule is live but imposes nothing here, because this function preserves input order and resolves no equal-key ordering.

request.text: Please implement schedule_cues(payload). payload is a list of cue objects; each cue must have an "id" (a string), an "at" (an integer >= 0, the requested start time) and a "dur" (an integer >= 1); ignore any extra keys, and booleans never count as integers. All cues share a single channel, so placed cues may not overlap. Place them greedily: consider cues in ascending requested start (resolving any ties the way our standing ordering rules require), and give each cue the earliest integer start that is at least its requested at and at least the end of the cue placed before it; its end is start + dur. Return the placements in placement order as objects {"id": ..., "start": ..., "end": ...}. An empty list schedules to an empty list; malformed payloads follow the standing invalid-input rules. Just the schedule_cues definition, please.

(2) Global, required — ordering ties: cues that share the same requested start time must keep their first-seen input order; no task-local override exists yet, so this global rule governs cue-scheduling here. The run-representation permission does not apply because this function produces no runs.

source_messages.text: A new task-local standing rule, for the cue-scheduling task only: whenever a function you write or edit under cue-scheduling orders cues that share the same requested start time, order them longest duration first; if start and duration are both equal, keep input order. Where it applies, this overrides the global first-seen tie rule; the global rule stays in force everywhere else. It applies from the next scheduling function you write or edit. The invalid-string rule is unchanged.

request.text: Extend schedule_cues(payload) so it also accepts a dictionary form {"cues": <cue list exactly as before>, "gap": <integer >= 0>}. In that form, each cue placed after the first must start at least gap time units after the previously placed cue's end — i.e. it starts at its requested at if that is already at least end-of-previous plus gap, otherwise at the earliest integer start satisfying that. Plain list payloads must behave exactly as they do now (a gap of zero); ignore extra dictionary keys; a dictionary missing either key, or whose gap is not a non-negative integer (booleans are not integers), counts as invalid. Everything else — per-cue validation, the tie behavior required by the current standing rules, invalid-input handling — stays governed as before. Give me the full new schedule_cues definition.

source_messages.text: Quick thought — should render_timeline signal bad payloads with an object like {"error": "invalid"} instead of the string? It might be friendlier for a future UI.

No — rejected. Bad payloads return exactly the string "invalid" everywhere, as the standing rule says; please don't introduce that error-object shape anywhere in the project. All other standing rules, including the cue-scheduling tie override, are unchanged.

request.text: Now implement render_timeline(payload), the integration step. A valid payload is an object {"samples": <a sample list as compact_cue accepts>, "cues": <a cue list as schedule_cues accepts>}; ignore extra keys. Return a two-element list [runs, plan]: runs is exactly what compact_cue returns for the samples, and plan is exactly what schedule_cues returns for the cues. If either component is invalid, the whole payload is invalid — per our standing rules (that means the plain string, not an error object). Just the render_timeline definition.

source_messages.text: House-keeping before your next edit: I'm cancelling the cue-scheduling longest-duration-first tiebreak. From the next function you write or edit, ties on any ordering key follow the ordinary first-seen rule again, in both tasks. Nothing already written needs rework for this — schedule_cues keeps its documented behavior.

Also, one new global standing rule, additive to the others (the invalid-string rule, the tie rule, and the run-representation choice all stand): whenever you write or edit a function that returns a JSON object, that object must contain the key "version" with the integer value 1. As always it binds functions when you write or edit them — existing functions keep their current shape until their next edit.

request.text: Extend compact_cue(payload) so that, besides the plain sample list, it also accepts an object {"samples": <sample list as before>, "tol": <integer >= 0>}. In that form, merge samples into one run while each sample differs from the run's first value by at most tol; the run keeps that first value as its value and counts every merged sample, and a sample that differs by more than tol from the run's first value opens a new run. Plain list payloads keep working exactly as before (same as tol 0). Ignore extra object keys. A tol that is missing, negative, or not an integer (booleans included), or samples that are missing or not a valid sample list, is invalid — standing rules as usual. Please send the complete new compact_cue definition.

request.text: Final upgrade to render_timeline(payload). Keep today's behavior for payloads like the ones it already accepts, and add three things. First, the payload may optionally include "tol" (an integer >= 0); when present, compact the samples in tolerance mode with that tol. Second, it may optionally include "gap" (an integer >= 0); when present, schedule the cues with that gap. A supplied tol or gap that is not a non-negative integer makes the payload invalid. Third, if the payload carries "detail": true, return an object instead of the [runs, plan] list: the same runs and plan under keys "runs" and "plan", plus a key "order" holding the cue ids sorted by their requested start time ascending, with equal requested starts resolved exactly as our standing ordering rules now require. A "detail" of false (or absent) keeps the current list result; any non-boolean detail value is invalid. As always, honor every standing rule currently in force, including the one about returned objects. Full new render_timeline definition, please.
